intro: AI literacy is baseline for a PM role now, not a specialisation. Draft content — check it before it ships as final.

topics.name: How LLMs work
topics.gist: A next-word predictor, not a database of facts.
topics.howItWorks: The model turns your prompt into tokens, then predicts the most likely next token, over and over.
need: It has no real understanding — it's pattern-matching from training data, so it can be confidently wrong.
Context window: everything the model can “see” at once. More context costs more money and time.
Fine-tuning changes the model's behaviour; retrieval (RAG) gives it fresh facts without retraining.

topics.name: When AI is the wrong solution
topics.gist: A model is the answer to some problems, not every problem.
topics.howItWorks: Rules and lookups are cheaper, faster and predictable — use them until the problem genuinely needs judgement.
need: If a simple rule or a database query solves it, an LLM adds cost and unpredictability for nothing.
AI is a bad fit where a wrong answer is expensive and hard to catch — legal, medical, financial calls.
Ask what error rate is tolerable before deciding whether AI is even in scope.

topics.name: Evaluating AI features
topics.gist: “It felt good in the demo” isn't an evaluation.
topics.howItWorks: Run the model against a labelled test set and score it before anyone sees a demo.
need: Precision: of what it flagged, how much was right. Recall: of what was actually true, how much it caught.
Hallucination: a confident, wrong answer. Measure how often it happens, not just whether it can.
Pick the metric that matches the cost of being wrong — a spam filter and a fraud model trade off differently.

topics.name: Cost and latency trade-offs
topics.gist: A bigger model is slower and costs more per answer.
topics.howItWorks: Every call to a model has a per-token cost and a response time that both grow with prompt size.
need: A smaller, cheaper model that's good enough usually beats the best model that's too slow or costly to ship.
Caching common answers and streaming the response both make a slow model feel faster.
Put a budget on it: cost per request, and what happens to margin at scale.

topics.name: Prompt design basics
topics.gist: The instructions matter as much as the model.
topics.howItWorks: A good prompt gives the model its role, the exact task, and an example of the output you want.
need: Show, don't just tell: one example of a good answer beats a paragraph of instructions.
Constrain the output format if downstream code has to parse it.
This is tunable, not fixed — know that before blaming the model for a bad first result.

topics.name: Metrics for AI products
topics.gist: Model metrics and product metrics are not the same thing.
topics.howItWorks: The model has an accuracy score; the product has a metric for whether it actually helped the user.
need: Track acceptance rate: how often a user keeps the AI's output instead of editing or rejecting it.
A model can hit its accuracy target and still fail the product if users don't trust or use it.
Watch for silent failures — a wrong answer nobody flags is worse than one that errors loudly.
